Novartis stock: FDA weighs tumor-risk action for gene therapies
sum: On November 6, 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration said it was investigating a serious malignancy risk linked to Novartis' gene therapies Zolgensma and Itvisma. The FDA safety communication said the review follows postmarketing reports of tumors in patients treated with Zolgensma.

The agency said three cases involved tumors associated with the GLI1 oncogene. In two cases, molecular analysis showed that DNA from the Zolgensma vector had integrated into the patients' genomes, with the construct inserted upstream of or within GLI1. The mechanism behind GLI1 overexpression in the third case remains under investigation.

The reports involved tumors in the central and peripheral nervous systems, spinal and paraspinal regions, and the kidney. The FDA said the risk applies to both onasemnogene abeparvovec products because Zolgensma and Itvisma use the same vector and construct. No neoplasia cases had been reported after Itvisma administration as of the agency's communication.

The FDA said the overall benefits of both therapies continue to outweigh their potential risks for approved uses. It is nevertheless evaluating whether regulatory action is appropriate and reviewing the adequacy of current prescribing information and Novartis' long-term follow-up safety studies.

Both products' U.S. prescribing information describes a theoretical risk of tumorigenicity from integration of AAV vector DNA into the genome. In the meantime, the agency said patients and clinical trial participants receiving the therapies should be monitored for tumor formation. The review creates a regulatory and safety issue for Novartis' gene-therapy portfolio, while the FDA's benefit-risk statement leaves the products' approved uses unchanged for now.

Novartis stock traded at 144.90 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:32 CET on Friday, November 13. Investors will watch the FDA's assessment of product labeling and long-term monitoring requirements alongside the company's pipeline updates.

sum: The US Food and Drug Administration is investigating a serious malignancy risk linked to Novartis' Zolgensma gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy. A safety alert dated Saturday, November 7, 2026, and published by the Hong Kong Department of Health reproduces the FDA's findings. Novartis stock traded at 145.84 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:43 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

The FDA said postmarketing reports involved tumors in the central and peripheral nervous systems, spinal and paraspinal areas, and the kidney. Three cases involved the GLI1 oncogene, which can promote cancer when overexpressed or abnormally activated.

In two cases, molecular testing found that Zolgensma's adeno-associated virus vector DNA had integrated into the patients' genomes. The therapy's promoter was positioned upstream of or within GLI1. The mechanism behind GLI1 overexpression in a third case remains under investigation.

The agency said the identified risk applies to Itvisma as well as Zolgensma because the products use the same vector and genetic construct. No neoplasia cases had been reported after Itvisma treatment at the time of the alert. The FDA is also monitoring comparable adeno-associated virus programs.

The FDA is assessing whether changes are needed to the prescribing information or to long-term follow-up requirements for the two products. Novartis is conducting long-term safety studies. Patients and clinical-trial participants receiving either therapy should be monitored for tumor formation.

The safety issue adds a regulatory overhang to Novartis' gene-therapy portfolio, although the FDA said the overall benefits of Zolgensma and Itvisma continue to outweigh their potential risks for approved uses. The review does not itself announce a label change, withdrawal or restriction.

sum: Legend Biotech’s shares tumbled 16% Tuesday following the CAR-T company’s third-quarter earnings report, marking a rocky debut for newly installed CEO Ingrid Zhang.
On the revenue side, sales from Carvykti, disclosed by partner Johnson & Johnson almost a month ago, reached $710 million in the third quarter, up from $657 million in Q2.

On the bottom line, Legend remained in the black after posting its first profit in Q2, recording an adjusted net income of $56 million in Q3, slightly down from $63 million in the three months ending in June.

Despite Carvykti’s growth momentum, Legend’s CFO Carlos Santos warned investors on a conference call Tuesday that Wall Street’s current sales consensus for 2027 sits “at the higher end of the scenarios that we’re currently anticipating.” Even though he said that double-digit year-over-year growth is still expected for the BCMA CAR-T next year, the more conservative projection likely put a damper on investor sentiment.
Santos attributed Legend’s reservation to launch delays outside the U.S. and, perhaps more alarming to investors, “a slower earlier-line share growth in the U.S.”

Investors have been concerned about Carvykti’s prospects in earlier multiple myeloma treatment settings because of competition from off-the-shelf bispecifics, including the BCMAxCD3 T-cell engager Tecvayli made by J&J.

Back in the second quarter, Legend’s stock price fell 10% after J&J’s then-innovative medicine chief, Jennifer Taubert, described the Tecvayli-Darzalex combo as having “the potential for cure” in second-line multiple myeloma.

Novartis Confirms Zolgensma Caused Tumors in Two Children Via Gene Therapy Vector Integration
sum: Nine tumor reports in SMA gene therapy patients reveal a risk the drug's FDA label still calls theoretical — raising urgent questions about post-market surveillance and what families of 6,000-plus treated children should do now

If your child received Zolgensma for spinal muscular atrophy, here is what you need to know today: Novartis has confirmed that the gene therapy's viral vector integrated into the DNA of two treated children and caused tumors — a risk the company's own prescribing information still describes as "theoretical" and says has not been causally established. The FDA label has not been updated to reflect these confirmed cases. Talk to your child's neurologist about whether tumor surveillance is warranted, particularly if your child was treated one to five years ago.

Novartis disclosed Thursday that nine children who received its blockbuster SMA gene therapy Zolgensma have since been diagnosed with tumors. In two of those cases, pathological analysis found direct evidence that the gene therapy's adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery vehicle had inserted itself into a patient's chromosomes — a process called insertional mutagenesis — and that this integration event was the likely cause of the tumor. Both confirmed patients received treatment for their tumors and are continuing to be monitored.

The disclosure, confirmed by STAT News, confirmed by BioSpace, reported by Endpoints News, and the SMA UK National MDT safety update dated November 4, 2026, is the first confirmed case of insertional mutagenesis causing tumors in patients treated with a commercially approved gene therapy. The confirmation also reveals a critical gap in the drug's existing prescribing information: Section 5.6 of Zolgensma's FDA label still states that "a causal relationship with ZOLGENSMA has not been established" — language that is now factually incorrect.
Novartis shares (NYSE: NVS ADRs) fell Thursday as investors weighed the implications for one of the company's most high-profile branded medicines.

Since Zolgensma's U.S. approval in May 2019, Novartis has received nine reports worldwide of tumors arising in previously treated patients. Of those nine reports, three children's tumors underwent pathological testing.

items.t: Novartis Faces a Reckoning: Three Trial Failures in Eight Days Test the Limits of Its Deal-Driven Gr
Novartis Shares Slide After Neuromuscular Candidate Acquired with Avidity Fails Phase III Trial
sum: Novartis shares fell the most in a single day since the COVID-19 pandemic after the pharma giant acknowledged that its neuromuscular candidate delpacibart etedesiran (del-desiran) failed a pivotal Phase III trial assessing the antibody oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC) in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1).

Del-desiran failed the Phase III HARBOR trial (NCT06411288) by missing the study’s primary endpoint of statistically significant improvement vs. placebo in video Hand Opening Time (vHOT) through week 54. vHOT is a frequently used measure of hand myotonia, according to a 2024 study, and involves clinical experts reviewing videos to measure the time from hand grip to opening.

However, Novartis added that it saw evidence of clinical activity in exploratory analyses and secondary endpoints—which included hand grip strength and quantitative Muscle Testing composite score, both measured by dynamometer; MD1 activity and participation scale; and 10-Meter Walk/Run Test. Safety findings from HARBOR were generally consistent with previously reported data, according to Novartis.

Novartis did not disclose details of its data but said it is evaluating the full dataset from the HARBOR trial and will engage with authorities to determine the most appropriate development path for del-desiran.

“Developing therapies for a complex disease like DM1 remains challenging, and setbacks are part of scientific progress,” Shreeram Aradhye, president, development and chief medical officer, Novartis, said in a statement. “As we continue to evaluate the full HARBOR dataset, we remain committed to identifying the most appropriate development path for the del-desiran program and advancing innovative approaches for people living with DM1 and other serious neuromuscular diseases.”

Del-desiran’s failure marked Novartis’ third clinical setback in a week. On Friday after the closing bell, the company and partner Ionis Pharmaceuticals acknowledged that their co-developed pelacarsen failed the Phase III Lp(a)HORIZON trial (NCT04023552) by missing its primary endpoint of reducing the risk, compared with placebo, of cardiovascular events—a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization requiring hospitalization.

Novartis stock falls nearly 4% as heart-drug failure deepens setbacks
sum: Novartis suffered a second trial disappointment within a week, after the Swiss pharma group’s potential blockbuster heart drug failed in a final-stage study.

The drug, pelacarsen, did lower levels of lipoprotein(a), a largely genetic risk factor for cardiovascular disease that affects roughly one in five people. However, that reduction did not translate into fewer deaths, heart attacks and strokes compared with placebo, the Swiss drugmaker said late on Sept 4.

The failure marks a major setback to hopes the medicine would open up a new approach to preventing cardiovascular disease. It also comes just days after Novartis temporarily paused trials of an experimental cell therapy for autoimmune diseases after three patients died.

Novartis shares fell as much as 3.9 per cent on Sept 7 in early Zurich trading, the biggest decline in over four months. They have gained 14 per cent so far this year. Amgen, which is developing a similar heart drug, fell almost 7 per cent in post-market trading on Sept 4.

“This questions whether any Lp(a)-lowering therapies can ultimately show a cardiovascular benefit,” according to Michael Leuchten, an analyst at Jefferies. Any negative reaction might be overstated, as even a successful trial would have raised questions over which patients would benefit and how well the drug could compete, he added.

Novartis is counting on a string of new medicines to sustain growth when some of its biggest products lose patent protection. Chief executive officer Vas Narasimhan has said successful late-stage trials could allow the company to raise its forecast for 5 to 6 per cent annual sales growth till 2030.

Analysts had seen pelacarsen as a potential blockbuster, with peak sales estimates ranging from about US$1.5 billion (S$1.9 billion) at UBS to US$5.4 billion at Jefferies, though the investment bank assigned the drug just a 30 per cent probability of success. Novartis had pegged the overall market opportunity at more than US$5 billion.

Investors are focused on pelacarsen, anti-inflammatory drug remibrutinib, and gene therapy del-desiran, as key drivers of the company's long-term growth as they could together generate more than $10 billion in peak annual sales, if approved. Pelacarsen is a subcutaneous injection given once a month that lowers lipoprotein (a) or Lp(a)- a type of genetically inherited cholesterol that has been linked to higher heart risk.

items.t: Novartis AG Stock (NVS) Moved Down by 3.14% on Jun 1: Key Drivers Unveiled
sum: Novartis AG (NVS) moved down by 3.14%. The Pharmaceuticals & Medical Research sector is down by 1.67%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Eli Lilly and Co (LLY) down 1.75%; Revolution Medicines Inc (RVMD) down 0.60%; Pfizer Inc (PFE) down 1.74%.

Novartis (NVS) experienced a decline in its share price today amidst a backdrop of mixed news and broader market pressures. While the company recently delivered encouraging updates regarding its pipeline, these positive developments appear to have been overshadowed by other factors.

Investor sentiment on the day was generally cautious, partly influenced by escalating geopolitical concerns related to a U.S.-Iran conflict, which led to a broader market downturn. Such macroeconomic and geopolitical events can often trigger significant intraday volatility and impact even fundamentally strong companies.

Adding to this, Novartis had recently announced early data from an experimental actinium-based radiopharmaceutical drug showing promising anti-tumor activity in prostate cancer. However, analysts also cautioned about the management of side effects, specifically high rates of dry mouth and severe anemia, which could introduce an element of risk regarding the drug's future development and adoption. This mixed assessment of a key pipeline asset may have contributed to investor unease.

Furthermore, upcoming domestic policy discussions in Switzerland, where Novartis is based, could be influencing investor sentiment. A looming referendum that proposes capping the country's population has reportedly caused alarm within the tech and pharmaceutical sectors, potentially signaling future operational challenges for companies reliant on international talent.

Earlier in the year, the company's first-quarter 2026 earnings indicated a miss on earnings per share forecasts, though revenue exceeded expectations. While Novartis later updated its full-year sales and profit guidance upwards, the initial earnings report, coupled with ongoing analyst discussions that present a range of price targets and recommendations, may still be contributing to uncertainty among some investors.

items.t: Novartis data at EULAR 2026 demonstrates momentum for broad immunology portfolio for complex, high unmet need diseases
sum: New Cosentyx® (secukinumab) data from REPLENISH, largest ever global Phase III trial in polymyalgia rheumatica, to be highlighted in oral session
New ianalumab interim results from Sjögren's Phase III extension study up to week 108 and Phase II data in systemic lupus erythematosus will be presented

Basel, June 1, 2026 – Novartis will present new data from 31 abstracts across its industry-leading immunology portfolio at the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Congress on June 3-6 in London, advancing scientific insight into high-burden autoimmune diseases.

"Novartis is committed to shaping the future of immunology. From small molecules to biologics and CAR-T cell therapy, our pioneering science is focused on where we can have the greatest impact on patient outcomes," said Angelika Jahreis, Global Head, Immunology Development, Novartis. "At EULAR, we will share compelling new data for Cosentyx, ianalumab and our CAR-T therapy rap-cel across diseases where there is high unmet need. These data demonstrate how Novartis innovation can have meaningful impact for people living with autoimmune diseases like polymyalgia rheumatica, Sjogren's disease, systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic sclerosis."

About Novartis Immunology At Novartis, we're advancing bold science with the goal of bringing relief and a renewed sense of hope to people living with autoimmune diseases. Building on our legacy of first-in-class innovation across rheumatology, dermatology and allergy, and a diverse industry-leading pipeline, we're committed to shaping what's next in Immunology.
